p01.reason: It denies rule A's twice-yearly rebase job that emailed organizers to re-save their series, and new.md nowhere tells its reader that such a job or email existed.

p02.reason: It excuses the reader from rule A's requirement that organizers re-save a series at the intended local hour after a transition, which new.md never presents.

p03.reason: It denies rule A's repeat interval counted in whole hours (a weekly series every 168 hours), and new.md never tells its reader that the interval was once fixed in hours.

p04.reason: It sets the organizer's choice against a zone guessed from the request's network address, an alternative neither old.md nor new.md presents anywhere.

p05.reason: It sets the shared job queue against cron entries on worker hosts, which neither document mentions; old.md also enqueued reminder jobs.

p06.licence: Some calendar products store each occurrence as a separate row as soon as a series is created.
p06.reason: It denies materialising occurrences, which new.md itself has just presented as what some calendar products do, and old.md did not materialise either.

p07.licence: The iCalendar standard allows a floating time that carries no zone at all.
p07.reason: It refuses floating times, which new.md has introduced in the preceding sentence, and it touches nothing of rule A.

p08.licence: The operating system zone files on a host can lag behind those releases by months.
p08.reason: It denies reading zone rules from the host, whose zone files new.md has presented in the preceding sentence; old.md shipped the same pinned copy, so this is not rule A.

p09.reason: It states a guarantee about reminders for cancelled or deleted occurrences, sets it against no other design and touches nothing of rule A.

p10.reason: It states the default when a reminder setting is absent, against no other design and without touching rule A.
